raw: {"analysis":"BTH directly addresses the 48-hour security review constraint by making the config file change a tracked critical-path item, and it preserves the existing two-signature policy. HKQ tries to avoid the config file entirely, which is cleaner but leaves a gap: it never explains how Gatekeeper will read the authoritative error budget data that currently lives in that SRE-owned file, so the core enforcement logic is under-specified. BTH also gives a more concrete rollback strategy tied to the config flag, whereas HKQ's flag rollback is vaguer.","verdict":"BTH"}
